questions.q: According to lesson 1, what should you do when a failure clearly was not your fault?
a: Take responsibility for getting back to success anyway
Wait until whoever caused it offers to compensate you
Refuse to move on until the damage is officially acknowledged
Treat the setback as proof that effort does not pay off
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the failure may not be yours, but how quickly you recover is up to you.

questions.q: In the ceramics class story, which group ended up making the better pottery?
a: The group graded on how many pieces it produced
The group allowed to make only one perfect piece
The group that studied theory before touching clay
The group that worked without any grading at all
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the quantity group produced better work because each piece carried less pressure.

questions.q: Why did making many pieces help the ceramics students improve?
a: Each failure taught them something they applied to the next piece
They had more time to copy the teacher's best example
They could pick the easiest clay to work with
They compared their work with the other group's
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that repeated attempts let them learn from every mistake and improve.

questions.q: What three things does Maxwell suggest working on to make the most of opportunities?
a: Clear goals, social skills and a positive mindset
Savings, credentials and a wide professional network
Luck, timing and a willingness to take big risks
Discipline, focus and an absence of distractions
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists clear goals, social skills and a positive mindset as the starting points.

questions.q: What did Greg Horn do after a flood destroyed his store?
a: He rebuilt it within weeks while still supporting his staff
He sold the ruined business and left the industry
He sued the city for failing to prevent the flooding
He reopened only after years of waiting for insurance
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes him scraping together the repair money and reopening in 21 days.
